answer: Picture an island whose only bridge is one sealed gate. Identity works like that gate: a key must live in its own distinct hardware chip that mints a hardware-bound secret, and each epoch answer a fresh challenge posted at a random vertex of the peer map. One chip cannot sign two divergent challenges, so copying it bricks the clone. A sybil farmer must buy M real devices and escort each through a slow, vendor-attested provisioning queue throttled per day. The attacker pays M physical chips plus queue delay, never M cheap signatures. That gate is the haven software swarms cannot fake.
